thread:
alyssa: Heads up — I'm seeing a surge of 5xx from a subset of inference nodes, started ~08:41 UTC. Logs show repeated `CUDA illegal memory access` followed by container restarts.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-01 — gpu-serving-5xx-spike (priority: P1) :rotating_light:
marco: roped in — which fleet/zone?
alyssa: gc-infer-prod-us-east-1, about 6/48 pods reporting OOM or `illegal memory access` in the last 3m. Node flaps observed on gke-gpu-12.
sanjay: I'm oncall, switching to this thread. First triage: are there kernel oops or just user-space crashes?
alyssa: initial stack in pod logs (truncated):
```
E tensorflow/core/common_runtime/executor.cc: Fatal CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
*** Caught signal: Segmentation fault (11) ***
[ 0] /usr/lib/libc.so.6(+0x3c5a0)
[ 1] /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11(+0x1a2b0) cudaCheckError
[ 2] /app/runtime/serve(+0x8f4b0) run_batch
[ 3] kernel: GPU pagewalk fault at address 0x7fffc12345 (misaligned)
```
marco: that `pagewalk fault` line is interesting — could be a driver/kernel-side paging race, not just model memory pressure.
emily: Customer impact: CS flagged a few customer requests failing for ~10m. I'm tracking the affected tenant ids and will update their status page.
ops-bot: Autoscaler observed 3 pods restart loops; scaling blocked due to quota.
sanjay: Immediate mitigations: 1) cordon nodes with repeated kernel pagewalk faults 2) migrate active pods off weakened nodes 3) force older driver kernel variant if available 4) enable canary fallback to cpu/quantized variant.
alyssa: Doing cordon + drain on gke-gpu-12, gke-gpu-14 now. Starting graceful migration for warmed caches.
marco: I'm collecting `/var/log/kern.log` and `dmesg` from the affected nodes and grabbing coredumps from the restarted containers (uploading to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2512345678/). Will also capture `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots.
deploy-bot: Rolling back last runtime patch on canary group (release: rtime-2026-04-21-3) -> triggered.
alyssa: After rollback, one node still shows `CUDA illegal memory access` and then a hard OOM kernel kill. Looks like two failure modes: user-space bad access then kernel escalation leading to node instability.
sanjay: Action items for night: - collect full vmcore if node panics - keep cordoned nodes drained - keep canary fallback enabled - escalate to kernel/driver team with logs + VM traces. I'm handing off to @sanjay — please pick up at 09:10 UTC.
marco: Repro attempt on staging failed so far. I reproduced a leak when running the same model with large batch windows and enabled continuous batching. Need to test misaligned pointer scenario with our custom attention kernel.
emily: Customer-success — pushed incident banner for impacted tenants, ETA for mitigation 30m. Logged affected request ids to the support ticket.
sanjay: Prioritizing stability: pin runtime to rtime-2026-04-21-1 for all production pools, temp disable continuous batching on sensitive pods, and throttle batch sizes.
ops-bot: Pin/patch applied to pool gc-infer-prod-us-east-1. Some requests now 200 again, error rate dropping from 12% -> 1.7% over last 8m.
alyssa: note — we saw a correlated spike in page faults before the illegal access stack trace. Hypothesis: a pagewalk race when the GPU driver and kernel SRM are simultaneously tearing down a KV cache entry. Escalating to driver team: @marco please attach steps to reproduce and all logs.
marco: attaching reproducer and dmesg snippets in follow-up message, requesting kernel driver triage and possible hotpatch.
incident-bot: Update: severity remains P1. Primary mitigation = rollback + node quarantine.
sanjay: Handoff summary for night oncall (sanjay): - current status: error rate degraded but under control; 2 nodes cordoned/drained - mitigation: rollbacks done, canary fallback on, continuous batching off - next: driver kernel triage, gather vmcore if panic, test reproducer in isolated infra - customer impact: intermittent 5xx for ~11m, now largely mitigated but still monitoring
customer-success: Thanks all — we'll keep customers posted. Please ping if ETA changes. :pray:
alyssa: leaving monitoring checks and log alerts for the night. If any node shows >2 kernel `pagewalk` faults within 15m, we auto-cordon.
sanjay: thanks team — taking over the oncall. If anyone sees recurrence, ping pager and this thread.
